name: Light Magenta
lede: Light Magenta joins the modifier *light* to [[magenta]], a crowd-survey name that, as photographed, has never appeared in our painting archive.

sections.title: A lightened primary
sections.body: The name follows the plain grammar of modifier plus base color, recorded in the xkcd 2010 crowd color survey [1]. The parent [[magenta]] itself names one of the three subtractive printing primaries, so Light Magenta is a paled version of a working color rather than a named shade with its own history [1]. The ISCC-NBS system's nearest block is "brilliant purple," an 11.5 Delta-E away, a wide gap that marks this crowd-chosen hex as brighter and pinker than the standards body's purple [1]. Nearest on file is [[ultra-pink]] at 2.9 units, with [[ultra-pink]] and [[purple-pizzazz]] close behind [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive has this color covering at least one per cent of its canvas, within a Delta-E of 4, as photographed [2]. That describes this archive's holdings, not the color in painting generally: a bright, crowd-named pink-purple like this rarely survives centuries of varnish and photography [2].

origin.named_after: the modifier light applied to the base color magenta
